name: Beat-grid element arrivals (sound marks information, not edits)

source.description: Four inspected music-led product films (batch 1, 2026-11-26) put their strong sound accents on a 1.00 s grid (about 120 bpm, every second beat), and each accent coincides with a new element arriving; scene changes carry no accent above chance. Measured with reference-corpus.py listen (signal features, not listening).

technique: Pick a tempo, put every element entrance on the beat grid, and give each arrival a short soft accent (pop, tick, knock) on the frame where it lands. Scene changes sit on other beats and are carried by picture (or a swell), not by a hit. The sound tracks the information the viewer should notice.
purpose: Make each new piece of information feel placed and audible; give a film without narration a steady, legible rhythm.
visual_behaviour: Words, chips, cards, ticks and counter steps arrive one per beat (0.5-1.0 s apart); each lands with a small settle; cuts fall between arrivals.
mechanics: beat = 60 / bpm (120 bpm -> 0.5 s). Arrival (end of the ease-out, or the overshoot peak) snaps to the grid with Studio.rhythm.snap; the entrance starts 0.2-0.4 s earlier. Accent SFX: onset on the arrival frame (earshot kit roles pop or knock, onset aligned), 3-10 dB over the bed. Cuts and section changes on whole bars without a hit; an impact or swell only at the 2-3 biggest turns. In the references the accents sit at x.55-x.60 s on a 1.00 s grid while hard cuts sit on whole seconds.

decomposition.timing: 120 bpm: arrivals every 0.5 or 1.0 s; sections every 4-8 s; accents 25-55 per minute in the references.

parameters.name: accent
parameters.description: SFX role for arrivals (pop, knock, tick)

failure_modes: With narration, the voice is the grid: snap arrivals to the spoken noun (studio.py words), not to the music, and keep accents quieter than the voice
An accent on every cut as well as every arrival makes everything equally loud
Arrival snapped at the tween start instead of where the element lands: the hit sounds early
Bright 5 ms blips read cheap against music; prefer rounded mid pops (earshot ui_pop family)

implementation.approach: Visual: Studio.rhythm.grid(bpm) and Studio.rhythm.snap for arrival times; entrances scheduled so they end on the grid. Sound: extract arrival cues (real-sfx from_hyperframes.py), render a kit with earshot kit (preset launch or crisp), place takes with onset on the cue frame, level against the bed with kit.gain_db; verify with earshot timeline --cues where the models are available, else reference-corpus.py listen numbers.

priority.note: Seen in 4 of 8 batch-1 references; drives the sound design of music-led films.

provenance.observed: Strong accents fall on a 1.00 s grid at x.55 s; each coincides with an element arriving (a word, an underline, a rule chip, a lock icon, a filled grid cell). The cuts at 13.65, 14.0 and 16.0 s have an accent within 100 ms in 1 of 6 boundaries (chance 0.10).
Accents land as the accent word and each of three problem cards arrive; from 11.59 to 23.59 s accents repeat every 1.00 s; hard cuts sit on whole seconds (10.0, 18.0 s) with no accent within 100 ms.
Accents repeat every 1.00 s from 3.55 to 15.56 s and from 25.57 to 33.55 s while UI steps and thumbnail grids build.
Accents repeat every 1.00 s from 0.56 to 3.55 s while the icon opens into the dashboard and the chart builds.
Accents at x.56-x.57 s on a 1.00 s grid (every second at 36.57-45.56 and 64.57-73.56 s) coincide with word slams and line arrivals; 12% of 25 boundaries carry an accent (chance 13%).
Six accents 0.28 s apart (1.00-2.37 s) coincide with app icons popping in around the title; 17% of 6 boundaries carry an accent (chance 20%).
Accents every 0.93 s (two beats at the 129 bpm estimate) from 15.53 to 21.15 s land with feature cards arriving.
Cuts at x.97 s, accents 0.56 s later at x.53 s every second, each on the card's UI action; only 9% of 23 boundaries carry an accent (chance 24%): accents avoid cuts.
Accents on a 0.48-0.49 s grid each bring one event: a dot appears, a line draws, a word settles, a letter fills, a circle blooms.
Accents about 0.5 s apart land on a rolling total's jumps and on metric cards switching.
List rows and carousel steps arrive 0.5 s apart, each on an accent; none of the 4 cuts carries one.
Each new archival image or word arrives on its own accent, 0.4-0.9 s apart.
The letters of the opening word slam into place 0.47 s apart, one per beat at about 129 bpm, each on an accent.

12 accents on a 1.00 s grid at x.65-x.70 s (1.65-12.70 s), each on an action (typing, loading-dot bounces, a card settling, the cursor press at 9.68 s); 0 of 7 boundaries carry an accent (chance 0.19).

14 accents on a 0.755 s grid (about 79.5 bpm), each on an element arriving (a green headline line, a card row, the Play button, a colour flood); 0 of 3 soft boundaries carry one (chance 0.14). The batch-1 rule at a slower tempo.
13 of 15 accents at x.55-x.57 s on a 1.00 s grid, each a new line or value arriving, while the cuts sit on whole seconds: the batch-1 split exactly.
Accents every 2.00 s (within 20 ms) plus off-beats 0.25 s later, each on a cursor press, drag or toggle; 0 of 3 boundaries carry an accent (chance 0.22).
Accents on a 1.00 s grid at x.05 s, each on an arrival (last letter, the full stop, the curve's start and its top); 0 of 4 boundaries carry one (chance 0.16).

Map counters tick on a 0.49 s accent grid (9.61, 10.10, 10.59 s); the three stat-card wipes sit 45-47 ms after onsets on a 1.00 s grid (5.36/5.41, 6.36/6.41, 7.36/7.41 s); 1 of 7 boundaries carries an accent (chance 0.14).
Facet arrivals sit on accents 0.63 s apart (2.55-4.44 s, one beat at 95.7 bpm) and then 0.30-0.33 s apart (5.04-8.80 s); 0 of 2 boundaries carry an accent (chance 0.19).

Accents at multiples of 0.24 s (123 bpm) land on interface arrivals: orbiting tiles (2.53, 3.02 s), cards (6.90, 7.13, 7.62, 7.85 s); here 3 of 6 boundaries also carry an accent (0.50 against chance 0.25).
Accents 0.46-0.49 s apart (129 bpm) from 2.39 to 7.08 s, each on an arrival (word settles, echoes, script word, badge, the O, tile swaps); 0 of 5 boundaries carry an accent (chance 0.12).
In the intro, accents on a 0.88-0.91 s grid with 0.44 and 0.23 s subdivisions land on chat and booking elements (6.27, 7.15, 8.06, 8.94, 9.85 s).
Accents on a 0.93-0.95 s grid land on each promise's proof (light bar 8.01 s, finished listing 8.96 s, card to icon 9.89 s, connectors 10.84 s); 0 of 5 boundaries carry an accent (chance 0.12).
Accents on a 0.25 s grid (phase x.05/x.30/x.55) land on arrivals after each wipe: the headline at 3.30 s, news cards stacking at 4.06, 4.30, 4.55 s; 1 of 9 boundaries carries one (chance 0.27).
Each morph lands on an accent 0.46-0.47 s apart (129 bpm); 0 of 7 boundaries carry an accent (chance 0.18).

combines_with.why: One drop before the biggest arrival makes it the loudest moment without raising levels.
Each UI state change is an arrival with its own accent.

licensing_notes: Technique only, measured from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown). No audio is copied; sounds come from the project's own kit.
